## Bump the plugin version in every change that touches the plugin

_critical · claude-code_

**Rule.** When a change touches anything under a plugin (skill, agent, hook, manifest), raise its `version` by semver in the same change: patch for wording and fixes, minor for a new skill, agent or capability, major for a removal or rename. To let users follow commits instead, leave `version` out of both layers.

**Why.** Claude Code caches a plugin by its version, and `claude plugin update` reports `already at the latest version` while the string is unchanged. A forgotten bump means the fix never reaches anyone who installed the plugin.

**Incorrect:**

```text
skills/hello/SKILL.md   edited
.claude-plugin/plugin.json   "version": "1.2.0"   (unchanged)
```

**Correct:**

```text
skills/hello/SKILL.md   edited
.claude-plugin/plugin.json   "version": "1.2.1"
```

## Keep plugin.json in .claude-plugin/ and every component at the plugin root

_critical · claude-code_

**Rule.** Save the manifest at `<plugin>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. Put `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `hooks/`, `.mcp.json` and every other component at the plugin root. Only `plugin.json` belongs inside `.claude-plugin/`.

**Why.** A `plugin.json` beside `skills/` may be ignored at install, and its `dependencies`, `displayName` and `agents` list go with it. A component folder inside `.claude-plugin/` never loads. SchemaStore also matches only `**/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, so editors give no validation for a root manifest.

**Incorrect:**

```text
my-plugin/
  plugin.json
  .claude-plugin/skills/hello/SKILL.md
```

**Correct:**

```text
my-plugin/
  .claude-plugin/plugin.json
  skills/hello/SKILL.md
```

## Ask for plugin settings through userConfig and mark secrets sensitive

_high · claude-code_

**Rule.** Declare every value the plugin needs from the user under `userConfig` in `plugin.json`, with `type`, `title` and `description`, and set `"sensitive": true` on tokens and passwords. Read them as `${user_config.KEY}` in MCP/LSP config and exec-form hook `args`, or as `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>` in hook processes.

**Why.** Instructions to edit `settings.json` by hand get skipped or leak a token into a committed file; a `userConfig` option opens a dialog at install and stores secrets in the platform's credential store.

**Incorrect:**

```markdown
Add `"MY_API_TOKEN": "..."` to the `env` block of your settings.json.
```

**Correct:**

```json
"userConfig": {
  "api_token": { "type": "string", "title": "API token", "description": "Token for the team API", "sensitive": true }
}
```

## Run plugin hook scripts in exec form, or double-quote ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}

_high · claude-code_

**Rule.** Reference bundled files as `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/...`. Prefer exec form (`command` plus `args`), where each element is one argument; in shell form wrap the path in double quotes.

**Why.** The install directory can contain spaces, and an unquoted path breaks into several words, so the hook fails only for some users; `claude plugin validate` warns about it.

**Incorrect:**

```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/format.sh" }
```

**Correct:**

```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "\"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/format.sh\"" }
```

## Name a plugin's MCP tools in full in hook matchers and permission rules

_high · claude-code_

**Rule.** In hook matchers, permission rules and `allowed-tools`, write a plugin MCP tool as `mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>`, or end the prefix with `*` to cover the server.

**Why.** A matcher on the server name or on `mcp__<server>__<tool>` never fires, so a guard on the tool silently does nothing.

**Incorrect:**

```json
{ "matcher": "mcp__db__query" }
```

**Correct:**

```json
{ "matcher": "mcp__plugin_my-plugin_db__query" }
```

## Give a version range to every dependency whose skills or tools your plugin calls

_high · claude-code_

**Rule.** Declare a dependency whose skills, agents or MCP tools you call in the object form with a `version` range you have tested, such as `~2.1.0`. Widen the range only after testing the newer release, in a new version of your plugin.

**Why.** A bare name follows whatever the marketplace publishes: the next release that renames a tool you call breaks your plugin on update, with no change on your side.

**Incorrect:**

```json
"dependencies": ["secrets-vault"]
```

**Correct:**

```json
"dependencies": [{ "name": "secrets-vault", "version": "~2.1.0" }]
```

## Keep name, version and dependencies identical in plugin.json and the marketplace entry

_high · claude-code_

**Rule.** When a value is set in both `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and the plugin's entry in `marketplace.json`, keep it identical: `name`, `version`, `author`, `license` and `dependencies`. Prefer setting `version` in `plugin.json` only.

**Why.** `plugin.json` wins for `version` at install, and `claude plugin tag` refuses a mismatch. Different names make `install <manifest-name>` fail with `not found in marketplace`. The browse view reads the entry, the installed view reads the manifest, so drift shows two different plugins.

**Incorrect:**

```json
// marketplace.json
{ "name": "formatter", "source": "./plugins/formatter", "version": "1.0.0" }
// plugins/formatter/.claude-plugin/plugin.json
{ "name": "code-formatter", "version": "1.1.0" }
```

**Correct:**

```json
// marketplace.json
{ "name": "formatter", "source": "./plugins/formatter" }
// plugins/formatter/.claude-plugin/plugin.json
{ "name": "formatter", "version": "1.1.0" }
```

## Read plugin files from CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT and write state to CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA

_high · claude-code_

**Rule.** Address bundled scripts and files through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` (or `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` inside a skill). Write caches, logs and anything that must survive an update to `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`. In hooks prefer the exec form with `args`, or wrap the variable in double quotes.

**Why.** `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` points at the cached copy of one version, which is replaced on update and removed later, so state kept there disappears. An unquoted path breaks as soon as it contains a space.

**Incorrect:**

```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/run.sh --log ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/cache.log" }
```

**Correct:**

```json
{ "type": "command", "command": "\"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/run.sh\" --log \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/cache.log\"" }
```

## Keep a skill description inside the 1,536-character listing limit

_high · claude-code_

**Rule.** Write the description as what the skill does, when to use it with real trigger phrases, and what it is not for, in at most about 1,000 characters. Move detail into the body.

**Why.** The skill listing truncates `description` plus `when_to_use` at 1,536 characters, so the trigger phrases or the `NOT for` clause at the end are the first to be lost, and the skill fires on the wrong requests or not at all.

**Incorrect:**

```text
description: <1,700 characters of workflow detail, then the trigger phrases, then NOT for …>
```

**Correct:**

```text
description: <what it does in one sentence>. Use when <trigger phrases>. NOT for <neighbouring skills>.
```

## List every agent file once the manifest sets agents

_high · claude-code_

**Rule.** When `plugin.json` sets `agents` (or `commands`, `outputStyles`, `workflows`), list every file the plugin ships, and add each new one in the same change. `skills` adds to the `skills/` scan, so a new skill folder needs no manifest edit.

**Why.** An agent file missing from an explicit `agents` array never loads, and nothing fails: the repo looks right and the agent does not exist at runtime.

**Incorrect:**

```json
{ "agents": ["./agents/reviewer.md"] }   // agents/tester.md exists too
```

**Correct:**

```json
{ "agents": ["./agents/reviewer.md", "./agents/tester.md"] }
```

## Tag a release for every version another plugin's dependency range points at

_high · claude-code_

**Rule.** When a plugin is a dependency with a version range, tag each release with `claude plugin tag <plugin-dir>`, which creates `<plugin>--v<version>`. Never let two plugins depend on each other; drop the preload instead.

**Why.** A range with no tag in range fails install with `has no git tag satisfying`, or leaves a relative-path plugin disabled. Dependencies install automatically, so a cycle installs both plugins whenever either is chosen.

**Incorrect:**

```text
"dependencies": [{ "name": "testing", "version": "^3.0.0" }]
git tag --list 'testing--v*'   # nothing
```

**Correct:**

```text
"dependencies": [{ "name": "testing", "version": "^3.0.0" }]
claude plugin tag plugins/testing   # Created tag testing--v3.0.0
```

## Treat a published plugin's name as permanent and relabel it with displayName

_high · claude-code_

**Rule.** Choose the kebab-case `name` once, before the first release, and keep it. Change what users see with `displayName`. When the name must change, rename the marketplace entry and `plugin.json` together and add the old name to the marketplace's `renames` map in the same change.

**Why.** Existing installs fail with `Plugin "<name>" not found in marketplace` the moment the old name disappears, because `enabledPlugins` and `pluginConfigs` still hold it.

**Incorrect:**

```json
// plugin.json, after release
{ "name": "code-formatter-pro" }
// marketplace.json: no renames entry for "code-formatter"
```

**Correct:**

```json
// plugin.json
{ "name": "code-formatter", "displayName": "Code Formatter Pro" }
```

## Run claude plugin validate and the drift check on every pull request

_high · claude-code_

**Rule.** In CI run `claude plugin validate --strict` on the marketplace and on each plugin directory (it does not read other plugins from the marketplace root), plus a drift check such as the `marketplace-creator` audit and a version-bump check against the PR base.

**Why.** Each of these breaks silently at install, not at commit: an unregistered plugin, an unlisted agent, a stale README, a change shipped without a bump.

**Incorrect:**

```text
CI: none — validated by hand before a release
```

**Correct:**

```text
CI: claude plugin validate --strict . && for p in plugins/*; do claude plugin validate --strict "$p"; done
    node check-marketplace.mjs . && node plan-release.mjs . --check --since origin/main
```

## List findings in one numbered table, worst first

_high · any_

**Rule.** Put every finding in one table ordered by severity, then by location, with the columns `#`, `Sev`,
`Where`, `Problem` and `Fix`, plus any column the skill needs (`By`, `WCAG`). Keep each cell to one
line. Where the surface renders file links, make `Where` a link to the file at the line. Past
fifteen rows, split it into one table per file or area under a small heading, numbering straight
through.

**Why.** Findings spread across headings and bullets cannot be scanned or compared, and the numbers are
what let the user answer "apply 1 and 4" instead of quoting the report back.

**Incorrect:**

```markdown
### Critical Issues

#### 1. Missing label
- **Location:** src/Form.tsx:12
- **Description:** The email input has no label.
- **Fix:** Add a label element.
```

**Correct:**

```markdown
| # | Sev | Where | Problem | Fix |
| :-: | :-: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 🔴 | `src/Form.tsx:12` | Email input has no accessible name | Add `<label htmlFor="email">` |
```

## Mark every status with the shared five-mark scale

_high · any_

**Rule.** Mark status with these five and nothing else: 🔴 broken or blocking, 🟡 costs the user and should
be fixed, 🔵 worth tidying, 🟢 nothing found, ⚪ not checked. Map the tool's own severities onto
them once, in the skill, and use the same marks in the verdict, the scorecard and the findings. The
verdict is the worst mark found.

**Why.** When every audit speaks its own dialect (critical, error, serious, warn, note), a reader moving
between reports cannot compare them, and without ⚪ an area that was never checked reads as passed.

**Exceptions.** A score with its own published thresholds, such as a Lighthouse category from 0 to 100, keeps
those thresholds and shows them as 🔴, 🟡 and 🟢.

## Open an audit report with a verdict line that quotes the tool's own summary

_high · any_

**Rule.** Start the report with one blockquote: the verdict for the worst finding, the count at each
severity, and the summary line the script or tool printed, quoted verbatim. Call a result clean
only when the tool's own exit code or summary says so.

**Why.** A report that opens with details makes the reader scroll to learn whether anything is wrong, and a
"looks clean" written from memory instead of from the tool's output is how a failing check ships.

**Incorrect:**

```markdown
## Audit results

I went through the skill and found a few things worth looking at.
```

**Correct:**

```markdown
## 🩺 Skill audit · `react/accessibility-audit`

> 🟡 **Needs work** · 0 errors · 16 warnings · 10 polish
> `0 error(s), 3 warning(s)` · `6 files · 101 body lines · 1116 ≈tokens · 5 references`
```

## Enforce a rule that must hold every time with a hook, not a skill

_medium · claude-code_

**Rule.** When the plugin must guarantee something on every tool call, such as never editing a protected file, implement it as a hook in `hooks/hooks.json` (or a mod). Use skills for guidance Claude applies when the task matches.

**Why.** A rule written into a skill holds only in sessions where that skill happened to load, so the protected file still gets edited in the others.

**Incorrect:**

```markdown
<!-- skills/safety/SKILL.md -->
Never edit files under migrations/.
```

**Correct:**

```json
{ "PreToolUse": [{ "matcher": "Write|Edit", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "\"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/deny-migrations.sh\"" }] }] }
```

## Narrow every plugin hook's matcher to the tools and events it is for

_medium · claude-code_

**Rule.** Give each `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` hook in `hooks/hooks.json` a `matcher` that names only the tools it handles, and exit early in the script for inputs that are not its concern.

**Why.** A hook with a broad matcher runs on every edit or command in every session that has the plugin enabled, slowing or blocking work the plugin has nothing to do with.

**Incorrect:**

```json
{ "PostToolUse": [{ "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "\"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/lint.sh\"" }] }] }
```

**Correct:**

```json
{ "PostToolUse": [{ "matcher": "Write|Edit", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "\"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/lint.sh\"" }] }] }
```

## Grade both the result and the skill firing, and add a case that must not trigger

_medium · claude-code_

**Rule.** In each eval case give one grader on the outcome (final message or produced file) and one `tool_used` grader on `Skill` with an `input_match` naming the skill. Phrase prompts as a user would, without the skill's name, and add at least one prompt that must not trigger it, graded with `min: 0`, `max: 0` and `arm: both`.

**Why.** A case that scores 1.0 with and without the plugin is not passing because of the plugin, and a description that over-triggers goes unnoticed without a negative case.

**Incorrect:**

```markdown
<!-- evals/review/prompt.md -->
Use /my-plugin:review on this diff.
```

**Correct:**

```markdown
---
type: tool_used
tool: Skill
input_match: '"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:[\w-]+:)?review"'
---
```

## Install the plugin from a local marketplace before pushing a release

_medium · claude-code_

**Rule.** Before each release, add the marketplace checkout with `claude plugin marketplace add ./`, install the changed plugin by `<plugin>@<marketplace>`, and confirm with `claude plugin list` and one skill run that it loads.

**Why.** `claude plugin validate` passes while the install still fails with `Source path does not exist` or a reserved-name refusal, so users meet the error first.

**Incorrect:**

```bash
claude plugin validate . && git push
```

**Correct:**

```bash
claude plugin validate . --strict
claude plugin marketplace add ./ && claude plugin install formatter@my-marketplace
claude plugin list   # Status: ✔ enabled
```

## Put instructions a plugin needs in a skill, not a CLAUDE.md inside the plugin

_medium · claude-code_

**Rule.** Ship guidance the model needs as a skill (`user-invocable: false` for background knowledge agents preload). Keep project instructions in the project's own `CLAUDE.md`, which a setup skill can write.

**Why.** `claude plugin validate` warns about a plugin-root `CLAUDE.md` because nothing reads it: the instructions in it never reach a session.

**Incorrect:**

```text
my-plugin/CLAUDE.md   "Always run the formatter after editing"
```

**Correct:**

```text
my-plugin/skills/format-rules/SKILL.md   user-invocable: false
```

## Keep SKILL.md under 500 lines and move reference material into references/

_medium · claude-code_

**Rule.** Keep `SKILL.md` to the steps and decisions every run needs, under 500 lines. Put tables, long examples and rare cases in `references/`, linked from the step that needs them with a note on when to open it. Put deterministic work in `scripts/`, which run without being loaded.

**Why.** A long `SKILL.md` is loaded whole on every invocation and re-attached after compaction only up to its first 5,000 tokens, so the steps at the end are the ones the model loses.

**Incorrect:**

```text
SKILL.md   900 lines: steps, every edge case, three full examples
```

**Correct:**

```text
SKILL.md   180 lines: steps
references/edge-cases.md   opened from step 4 when the input is unusual
```

## Put hooks and MCP servers in the plugin, never in plugin agent frontmatter

_medium · claude-code_

**Rule.** Declare hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` (top-level `"hooks"` key) and MCP servers in `.mcp.json` at the plugin root. In a plugin agent's frontmatter use only the keys Claude Code reads for plugin agents.

**Why.** Claude Code drops `permissionMode`, `hooks`, `mcpServers` and `initialPrompt` from agents shipped in a plugin, so they promise behaviour that never happens.

**Incorrect:**

```text
agents/reviewer.md
---
name: reviewer
hooks: { PostToolUse: … }
---
```

**Correct:**

```text
hooks/hooks.json
{ "hooks": { "PostToolUse": [ … ] } }
```

## Start every component path with ./ relative to the plugin root

_medium · claude-code_

**Rule.** Write every component path in `plugin.json` and every relative `source` in `marketplace.json` as `./…`, relative to the plugin (or marketplace) root, with forward slashes. Reference files at run time through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`.

**Why.** `commands/foo.md` fails validation, `..` is rejected as path traversal, and a backslash path is rejected on macOS and Linux. An absolute path breaks once the plugin is copied into the cache.

**Incorrect:**

```json
{ "agents": ["agents/reviewer.md"], "hooks": "../shared/hooks.json" }
```

**Correct:**

```json
{ "agents": ["./agents/reviewer.md"], "hooks": "./hooks/hooks.json" }
```

## Show a scorecard when the audit covers a fixed set of areas

_medium · any_

**Rule.** When the audit checks the same areas on every run (categories, plugins, URLs, checklist sections),
put a table right after the verdict with one row per area: the area, its worst mark and its
counts. The skill fixes the rows and their order; an area that was not checked stays in the table
marked ⚪.

**Why.** Without a scorecard the reader rebuilds the overall picture from the findings list, and a row that
silently disappears hides an area nobody checked.

**Correct:**

```markdown
| Area | Status | Found |
| --- | :-: | --- |
| Frontmatter | 🟢 | — |
| Description & routing | 🟡 | 1 warning |
| Bundled files | ⚪ | no scripts or assets |
```

## Give a detail block only to findings whose fix will not fit the table, at most five

_medium · any_

**Rule.** Below the findings table, add a `### <n> · <mark> <claim>` block with the quoted evidence and a
diff or before/after only for 🔴 and 🟡 findings whose fix does not fit in the `Fix` cell. Write at
most five, choosing the findings that cost the reader most; findings on the same lines share one
block (`### 1–3 · 🟡 …`). Every other fix is written out when it is applied.

**Why.** A diff under every finding makes the report longer than the thing it audits, and the reader gives
up before reaching the findings that matter.

## Close an audit report with what was not checked and the one next step

_medium · any_

**Rule.** End the report with two lines. **Not checked:** what this run could not cover, and the skill or
step that covers it. **Next:** the one action expected from the user, such as the finding numbers
to apply or the command to run. Anything else the reader should know about the run (a fallback,
findings dropped or merged, a cap) goes in a single line just above them.

**Why.** A report that is silent about what it skipped reads as a pass for everything, and one that ends
without a next step leaves the user guessing whether anything was already changed.

**Correct:**

```markdown
**Not checked:** drawing and hotkeys need a live session → run `claude --plugin-dir .`

**Next:** nothing is applied yet. Reply with the numbers to apply (`1 3`) or `all`.
```

## Report a clean run as the heading and one line

_medium · any_

**Rule.** When the audit found nothing, the report is its heading and one 🟢 line carrying the tool's
summary as evidence. Leave out the scorecard, the findings table and any list of checks that
passed.

**Why.** A clean report padded with every check that passed teaches the reader to skim, and they then skim
the next report, the one with a real finding in it.

**Correct:**

```markdown
## 🩺 Marketplace doctor · `szum-tech`

> 🟢 **Clean** · 15 plugins · 0 errors · 0 warnings · `✓ 0 errors  ⚠ 0 warnings`
```

## Write new slash commands as skills under skills/, not as commands/ files

_low · claude-code_

**Rule.** Add each new command as `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Keep `commands/` only for files moved unchanged from a `.claude/commands/` setup.

**Why.** A `commands/` file cannot bundle supporting files and is the legacy form, so it has to be migrated the first time it grows.

**Incorrect:**

```text
commands/deploy.md
```

**Correct:**

```text
skills/deploy/SKILL.md
```

## Open every plugin.json and marketplace.json with a SchemaStore $schema

_low · claude-code_

**Rule.** Make `$schema` the first key: `https://www.schemastore.org/claude-code-plugin-manifest.json` in `plugin.json` and `https://www.schemastore.org/claude-code-marketplace.json` in `marketplace.json`.

**Why.** Without it a typo such as `"agent"` for `"agents"` is stripped silently at load and only `claude plugin validate` would notice. A guessed URL that returns 404 gives no help either, so use the published ones.

**Incorrect:**

```json
{
  "name": "my-plugin"
}
```

**Correct:**

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://www.schemastore.org/claude-code-plugin-manifest.json",
  "name": "my-plugin"
}
```

## Write reports in GitHub-flavoured Markdown without HTML

_low · any_

**Rule.** Build the report only from what every surface renders: headings, tables, emoji, blockquotes, bold,
links and fenced code. Leave out HTML such as `<details>` or styled spans, ANSI colour codes, and
diagrams that need a renderer.

**Why.** The same report is read in the desktop app, in a terminal and in a pull-request comment, and HTML
that one of them does not render shows up there as raw tags.
